children: heads into Tuesday's results with a bigger test: can processors and AI accelerators deliver growth together? Shares rose 0.76% to $508.62 at 9:35 a.m. ET on November 2. A TipRanks preview puts the spotlight on Susquehanna's $74 billion forecast for 2027 data-center revenue, split between $33 billion from server CPUs and $41 billion from GPUs.

That puts GPUs at roughly 55% of the projected total, making accelerator deliveries a major test of the growth case. The report lists $650 price targets from both Susquehanna and Jefferies. For the quarter being reported, AMD has guided to $13 billion in revenue, plus or minus $300 million, and approximately 56% adjusted gross margin. Tuesday's margin, next-quarter guidance and evidence of sustained Helios shipment growth could determine how much confidence those forecasts deserve.

The GuruFocus snapshot highlights the valuation hurdle. AMD scores 82 out of 100, with growth and momentum standing out, while GF Value is its weakest dimension. A price-to-earnings ratio of 130.52 suggests investors are already paying for substantial earnings growth. Strong business performance could support that premium, but brokerage projections still need to become revenue and profit.

title: AMD Stocks Edge Higher With Earnings Testing a $74 Billion Data-Center Forecast
